Header: Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris Muozo mweusi in Swahili

Prevention: Crop rotation with non-brassica crops for at least 2 years (such as maize, legumes, tomatoes).
Avoid overhead irrigation because the water splashes back from the ground to the plant can carry the disease.
Avoid flood/furrow irrigation because it will carry the disease from infected to uninfected areas.
Avoid standing water and apply mulch to reduce splashes.
Grow cabbage on raised beds to reduce black rot incidences
Remove crop debris after harvesting and feed to animals.
Do not leave or bury in the field.
Use disease-free seeds from a certified agro-input dealer
Monitoring: V shaped lesion on the leaves which are initially light brown, but later turn dark brown.
The veins on the cabbage leaves become black
Cross sections of infected stems reveal a black ring
In later stages, heads turn black with an offensive foul smell.
If 3 – 5 young plants show symptoms / acre consider taking action.
However, if slight symptoms of the disease occur at a late growth stage of cabbage or close to harvest, no chemical action is needed, as the few damaged outer leaves can just be removed.
Direct Control: Prevention is the most effective control measure for bacterial diseases.
Uproot the infected young plants and feed to animals.
Do not leave or bury in the field.
Avoid movement through the field when plants are wet to prevent disease spread
Restrictions: Copper-based compounds such as copper oxychloride (such as
WP at 40 – 80gm/20 litres of water but double-check product label; or
Mo-Copper50WP; Royalcop50WP; Sulcop50DF; Coprado50WP; Cupravit50WP and others).
This can help to some extent to suppress bacterial blight infections, but it cannot completely control the disease.
It is a multi-side action bactericide.
Never spray more than 6 kg copper per ha per year !
II (moderately hazardous) but very toxic to aquatic organisms so don’t spray near water source.
Pre-harvest interval (p.h.i.) 7 days; restricted re- entry interval (r.e.i.) 1 day after spray.
When used too much, copper(II)-ions can accumulate in soil and water.
Do not use during fruit set
